body:
# the contributor audit of the new simplex stability dependencies

All three sources below were read in full. Their mathematical statements
and constants pass; exact verifiers were rerun. None is an OC theorem.

## Critical simplex vertex averaging

`candidate c6aadce19d219a98` constructs a
genuine martingale with the prescribed critical vertex-average and
uniform marginals. The minimum-coordinate cells partition off finitely
many null hyperplanes. Their masses are1/d under each law. The radial
parameter is independent of the lower-facet law because the threshold
test is exactly independent of that parameter at b=1/d. The density
normalizers d*((d-1)/d)^(d-1) and (d-1)*((d-1)/d)^(d-2) agree.

The lower-dimensional merging lemma is proved by direct conditional
density integration and applies also when the lower simplex is a point.
Reconstructing with the same minimum label and value gives the uniform
full marginal and the conditional mean identity by the tower property.
The argument does not pretend to keep the original independent input
coupling. Smaller steps follow by pointwise interpolation with that
original input, and the minimum function gives strict failure at EVERY
larger step. The corrected optional random-step uniqueness statement
is appropriately restricted and is unused. Verifier3189 PASS; the
independent degeneracy audit was received and agrees.

## Minimum enclosing simplex and centered facet contacts

`candidate 783495094e97ee67` excludes
escaping vertices by an actual cone inside each enclosing simplex.
Compact vertex tuples preserve the contained positive-volume body,
so the limit is still a simplex and determinant continuity attains
the minimum. If a facet centroid is outside its compact contact set,
strict separation yields an explicit tilt that stays feasible by a
uniform contact-neighborhood margin. The exact volume derivative is
negative. This proves contact without any differentiability or
constraint qualification.

The inner and outer simplex support comparisons and their volumes are
correct. An outlying point cones over an inner facet with disjoint
interior from the inner simplex; its exact volume controls every
coordinate and their sum. The binomial and Bernoulli estimates give
the claimed linear Hausdorff bound. Maximizing coordinates and minimizing
their sum select d+1 distinct vertices, with the stated matching bound.
Their averages give the corresponding facet centroids. Dimensions1 and
zero Hausdorff distance are treated. Verifier95actualtilts/280constants/
123matching cases PASS.

## Convex facet strips and relative cap-loss errors

`candidate e499db59e12bfbe4` uses a convex
conditional slice average and the exact beta coordinate density. The
fixed interior averaging interval and Bernoulli weight comparison give
the strip constant without a supremum/integral bound. The case of an
interval facet is explicitly included.

The gauge is convex and finite because the body contains a homothetic
inner simplex. Its facet restriction minus1 is nonnegative and convex;
facet-centroid contact gives its zero when present. The exact geometric
series controls radial missing-volume weight with the exponent d, and
the centroid facet cones have equal mass1/(d+1). A cap disagreement is
in a thin canonical strip; the ray identity divides its width by the
retained radial scale with no additive location error. Summing the
disjoint facet-cone missing volumes introduces no extra factor. Ordinary
hyperplane and cone-boundary nullity is sufficient for all closed caps.
Verifier6264strip/1045radial/72actualmissingcap checks PASS.

These checks support the new all-dimensional local ordinary proof.
The separate quantitative functional source has an independent full
functional audit, whose verifier8096 was also rerun successfully.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
